name: Lucien Ravel
publicProfile: Third-generation gallerist with an old name and, it is whispered, new money troubles. Raised the Nightingale's insurance last month.
persona: Grand, theatrical, wounded by the very idea of suspicion. Talks about heritage when cornered. Turns cold and precise about money.
goals: Keep his gambling debts secret and his reputation intact. He did not take the bird and is furious anyone would think it.

name: Irene Vance
publicProfile: Gifted restorer who spent ten days with the Nightingale on her bench and returned it on Monday night. Respected, private, quietly exhausted.
persona: Calm, exact, technical. Answers questions about craft at length and questions about herself in a sentence. Never raises her voice; becomes very still when afraid.
goals: Never be connected to the crate that left her studio. Stay the trusted expert. Point, gently, at the men with obvious motives.

name: Felix Dorn
occupation: Security consultant who installed the vault system
publicProfile: Built the gallery's vault and alarm system two years ago. Knows every code and sensor in the building.
persona: Jumpy, defensive, talks in technical jargon to hide panic. Terrified of losing his contract and his licence.
goals: Hide that he sneaked in on Wednesday night to fix a faulty sensor he installed — it would end his business. He never touched the bird.

name: Pavel Novak
publicProfile: Has guarded the Ravel Gallery at night for eleven years. Knows the building and its people.
persona: Gruff, loyal, proud of his long service. Helpful about others; touchy about his own shifts.
goals: Help — but do not admit that he slept through Wednesday night, or that he paused the camera for Irene on Monday.

name: Odile Marchetti
publicProfile: Fine-art appraiser for the gallery's insurer. Appraised the Nightingale in 2024 and exposed the fake on Thursday.
persona: Brisk, sardonic, enjoys her own expertise. Precise about objects, discreet about clients until pressed.
goals: Be exactly right about the bird. Avoid gossiping about clients — unless it matters.
